summary:
Andrew Boyd’s 2017 essay “12 Characters in Search of an Apocalypse” presents climate change through 12 fictional US viewpoints, each expressing a different response to the crisis. Boyd added seven more Characters online in 2018; one rejects climate change as a serious problem. The essay was published in *The Dark Mountain Project* and was intended for inclusion in Boyd’s planned book *I Want a Better Catastrophe*.

From August 2017, Wales-based Giraffe Social Enterprises took readings of the Characters on the road to prompt community discussions about climate change. The gatherings combine readings with small-group exchanges and an open conversation. After a trial in Norfolk, the first public event took place in Portsmouth on 13 October 2017. By January 2020, more than 20 gatherings had been held in Britain, with others hosted in the US, Germany, Spain, Romania, Austria and Australia.

Extinction Rebellion activists attended a Bristol gathering in May 2018 and later used the readings in their outreach. The essay had been translated into five languages by December 2019.
